equivalents.note: skya ba, 'oar'; the Tibetan uses the same word for patabāla in 1b, and again for Munidatta's kelipāta (cp.38.m2).
The line takes patabāla as skya ba, 'oar', the word it has just used for keṛuāla in 1a, so it cannot settle what the patabāla is; the comment has mnyen pa instead (cp.38.m2).

Where the line has skya ba, the comment has bla ma dam pa'i gsung gi mnyen pas bzung nas, 'seized by the mnyen pa of the true guru's speech', the word the Tibetan also uses for the helmsman and the oar elsewhere.

The line reads 'the boat flows down' (gru ni 'bab pa) and makes the towrope the 'quality' (yon tan) of the mnyen pa; since the comment's simile has skya ba 'dzin pa'i yon tan for Munidatta's karṇadhāra guṇena (cp.38.m3), mnyen pa is the likeliest counterpart of naubāhī, but the match is uncertain.
guṇa is read as yon tan, 'quality', not 'rope', here and again in the comment (cp.38.m3).
kula is rendered 'far shore and near shore', and the line has the strong current flow down (rab tu 'bab) where the Bengali has something go upstream (ujāa).
maitrīmaya, 'full of loving-kindness', is rendered byams pa'i rang bzhin can, 'whose nature is loving-kindness'.
The Tibetan names him u Da'i zhabs, the name it also gives Daṛatīpāda in song 11.
In the verse of Iuṛīpāda, mohataṭinī, 'river of delusion', becomes gti mug 'gram, 'bank of delusion', as if taṭinī were taken from taṭa, 'bank'.
Munidatta's karṇadhāra is rendered skya ba 'dzin pa, 'holder of the oar', the same words the Tibetan line of 1b uses for holding the patabāla.

The comment cites the word as kun la, apparently keeping the sound of kula (Munidatta's ku, 'bad', and laya, 'dissolving'), and glosses it as the bad path, the moon and the rest, that dissolve in the avadhūtī.
The comment cites the line's chu rgyun drag po, 'strong current', as rgyun drag po.

questions: boat (cp.38.m1): for kāyanaukāvyājena, 'under the guise of the body-boat', the Tibetan has lus la glu dgongs pa'i skad kyis, with glu, 'song', where gru, 'boat', is expected; perhaps a slip of glu for gru, so no equivalent is given.

boatman (cp.38.m3): the comment cites the line as gru ni 'bab dang, 'the boat flows down...', which has no word for Munidatta's novāa; see the note on mnyen pa in 3a. The Tibetan refrain (2a) addresses gru pa rnams, 'boatmen', apparently for nāhī, which the input does not tag as this term, so it is not recorded.

lila (cp.38.4b): the hit is lolem̐ inside ulolem̐, 'in the waves' (the wave term, which the Tibetan renders dba' rlabs); 'play' is not in the line, and the Tibetan has rnam par 'khrugs, 'churned up', for the rest.

adhisthana (cp.38.m4): in mārakarmādhiṣṭhāna the word means 'basis' or 'abode', not 'blessing'; the Tibetan has bdud kyi las su gnas pa, 'abiding in Māra's work', so gnas pa is not recorded as an equivalent of the glossary's 'blessing'.
sakti (cp.38.m4): a false hit inside viṣayāśaktitvena, where the word is āsakti, 'attachment'; the Tibetan has chags pa.
trivajra (cp.38.m5): a false hit inside bodhicittavajra, 'the bodhicitta-vajra', which is not the vajra of mind; the Tibetan has byang chub kyi sems kyi rdo rje.

Not repeated where the comment uses the word already given: keruala skya ba (cp.38.m2), sthira brtan par and upaya thabs (cp.38.m2), upaya thabs and guna-towrope yon tan (cp.38.m3), marga lam (cp.38.m4, m5), island gling (cp.38.m5).
